scope: Read-only audit of MEMOTE 0.17.0 SBO and annotation checks against the unmodified published iMcBath SBML. No model/repository modifications.
summary: Ten of eleven installed SBO tests invert the expected success predicate: their data are MISSING/nonmatching components, yet the assertion demands missing_count == total_count. Biomass alone correctly demands zero.
The defect is also present in the official MEMOTE 0.17.0 source fetched online, not an inference from test output alone.

Four of five SBO failures contain both real metadata gaps and inverted assertions; biomass is a normal metadata failure. Six SBO passes are false passes with 100% of the expected annotations missing/nonmatching.

Do not subtract four failures and declare the model corrected: those four still have missing annotations, while the six false passes reveal additional gaps. Preserve raw audit results and explain interpretation separately.
General annotation tests have no analogous inverted assertion. Fourteen wrong_ids failures stop because an entire namespace is absent; they do not report malformed identifiers.
EcoGene, CCDS and HPRD direct gene-identity annotations are outside organism scope. Absence is expected, and their associated wrong_ids preconditions should not be described as biological errors.

sbo_cases.finding: 858 of 879 SBML-loaded species have no SBO key; 21 have SBO:0000247. The underlying metadata gap is real despite the inverted assertion.
772 of 913 SBML-loaded reactions have no SBO key. Of the 141 annotated reactions, 98 use generic SBO:0000375 (process), and 43 use SBO:0000627 (exchange reaction).
All 730 gene annotations are empty. The reported pass is a false pass caused by the inverted assertion.

All 721 detected pure metabolic reactions lack the exact expected term. 668 have no SBO and 53 have generic SBO:0000375. The pass is false; the count includes both absent and insufficiently specific terms.

All 122 detected transport reactions lack an accepted transport term. 77 have no SBO and 45 have generic SBO:0000375. The pass is false. The message also incorrectly labels transport reactions as metabolic/biochemical.

858 species lack SBO:0000247; none of those 858 has another SBO. The failure message incorrectly calls these transport reactions. A blanket simple-chemical annotation needs semantic review for macromolecular/lumped species; this checker tests exact strings rather than ontology relationships.
All 730 genes lack SBO:0000243. The pass is false; this does not imply the model has no genes or GPR rules.

Exactly EX_ch4_e, EX_co_e, EX_fol_e, EX_ham_e, and EX_n2_e lack the expected exchange term. The other 43 of 48 detected exchanges have it. The failure has a real metadata basis even though the assertion is inverted.
All 12 detected demands lack SBO:0000628 and have no SBO. Reported pass is false. The first docstring line wrongly says SBO:0000627, but code uses 0000628; the message also wrongly says genes.
The one detected sink, SK_cyan_c, has no SBO:0000632 or other SBO. Reported pass is false. The message wrongly says genes.
BIOMASS_Mcapsulatus lacks SBO:0000629. This test correctly asserts zero missing terms and is a genuine annotation failure, without the inversion defect.

Samples mix KEGG Drug identifiers beginning D with Compound identifiers beginning C under kegg.compound. This is namespace/format nonconformance, not proof that the biological compound has no database record.
Samples contain leading spaces in secondary cpd identifiers. This is an actual string-format problem in the model annotation.
The test fails at the precondition assert len(total) > 0 before running any ID regex check. This failure documents zero annotations in the namespace, not invalid existing identifiers.
Samples contain serialized-list punctuation and literal ' text within CHEBI identifiers. This is malformed metadata.

All 382 annotated species fail the local regex; samples use REACTOME:419151-style values rather than accepted stable-ID syntax, and some contain serialized lists. Local regex nonconformance is proven; whether each historical identifier can resolve was not checked.
2omhmbl_c uses the descriptive name 3-demethylubiquinol-8 as the identifier instead of an MNXM accession.

Samples use older hyphenated strings such as 26dap-LL where the installed regex permits letters, digits and underscores. This is recorded format nonconformance; mapping each legacy identifier to a current accession requires separate verification.
Samples contain serialized-list punctuation or descriptive prose such as an oxidized c-type cytochrome in the ID field.
NO3R1 has multiple numeric identifiers merged with colon and literal ' separators as one string.

cross_format_caveat: The source JSON stores ontology annotations under uppercase SBO; the audited SBML is loaded by COBRApy with lowercase sbo and contains 21 annotated species plus 141 annotated reactions. Checking raw JSON for lowercase sbo would falsely report zero. Audit interpretations here use the SBML path recorded by run-metadata.
limitations: The audit checks metadata semantics and installed source behavior; it does not validate biological predictions.
No remote identifier lookup or remapping was performed. Regex mismatch alone is not proof a biological record is absent.
Ontology exact-term checks are more restrictive than general semantic validity; specific complex species should be curated according to their represented entity.
No corrected MEMOTE score or changed test suite has been produced.
